sections.title: Advanced Concept of Embedded Figures
sections.content: At Level 2, figures are more complex and may involve overlapping shapes or grid-based constructions. You must mentally build the complete structure from the description and then identify hidden shapes such as trapeziums, parallelograms, or multiple triangles.

sections.title: Overlapping Shapes Concept
sections.content: Example: An equilateral triangle with an inverted equilateral triangle placed inside it, forming a 6-pointed star, and the entire figure is enclosed in a circle. Step 1: Visualize a large equilateral triangle. Step 2: Place another inverted triangle of the same size inside it. Step 3: Observe the central hexagon and surrounding smaller triangles. Step 4: Now check for embedded triangles, parallelograms, or trapeziums formed by intersecting lines.

sections.title: Grid Pattern Construction
sections.content: Example: A 4x4 grid of dots where all adjacent dots are connected horizontally and vertically. Step 1: Visualize 4 rows and 4 columns. Step 2: Identify small 1x1 squares. Step 3: Combine adjacent squares to form rectangles. Step 4: Look for larger rectangles and possible parallelograms if diagonals are mentioned.

sections.title: Identifying Trapeziums and Parallelograms
sections.content: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides. A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides. In grid-based figures, check parallel lines first. Then verify if four sides form a closed figure with required parallel properties.

sections.title: 3–4 Step Solved Example 1
sections.content: Question: How many rectangles are embedded in a 3x3 square grid? Solution: Step 1: Count all 1x1 squares. Step 2: Count 1x2 and 2x1 rectangles. Step 3: Count 2x2 squares and 3x1 rectangles. Step 4: Add all counts carefully to get the total number of rectangles.

sections.title: 3–4 Step Solved Example 2
sections.content: Question: How many small triangles are formed in a hexagram (two overlapping equilateral triangles)? Solution: Step 1: Count the 6 outer small triangles. Step 2: Count the central overlapping triangles. Step 3: Identify medium-sized triangles formed by combining smaller ones. Step 4: Add all triangles systematically.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Ignoring rotated or tilted shapes. 2. Counting only smallest shapes. 3. Forgetting larger combinations. 4. Not checking parallel sides properly.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 requires structured counting and strong visualization. Always build the figure step-by-step, identify intersections, and count shapes from smallest to largest.

tricks.title: Small to Large Counting Strategy
tricks.explanation: Always count the smallest shapes first, then medium, then large ones.
tricks.example: In a grid, count 1x1 squares before 2x2 squares.

tricks.title: Parallel Line Detection
tricks.explanation: Identify sets of parallel lines to detect trapeziums or parallelograms.
tricks.example: Opposite sides in a rectangle are parallel.

tricks.title: Intersection Focus
tricks.explanation: More intersecting lines mean more hidden shapes.
tricks.example: Overlapping triangles create multiple small triangles at the center.

tricks.title: Combination Method
tricks.explanation: Combine two or more small shapes to detect larger shapes.
tricks.example: Two adjacent small triangles can form a larger triangle.

tricks.title: Row and Column Logic
tricks.explanation: In grids, choose pairs of rows and columns to form rectangles.
tricks.example: Selecting top and bottom rows forms different rectangle heights.

tricks.title: Tilted Shape Awareness
tricks.explanation: Do not ignore slanted shapes inside the figure.
tricks.example: A diamond shape inside a square may form a parallelogram.

tricks.title: Systematic Listing
tricks.explanation: List each type of shape separately to avoid missing any.
tricks.example: List all trapeziums first, then parallelograms.

tricks.title: Recheck Total Count
tricks.explanation: After counting, verify once again from a different angle.
tricks.example: Rotate the mental image and re-evaluate larger shapes.
